question_design_notes.mistake_definition: A mistake is an unsafe, inappropriate, poorly timed, or insufficiently anticipatory driving decision or action. A mistake may occur even when no formal traffic-rule violation, collision, or lane violation occurs.
question_design_notes.infraction_definition: An infraction is a concrete traffic-rule violation or prohibited event that actually occurred, such as entering against a red light, failing to stop, violating a lane boundary, leaving the roadway, or causing a collision.
question_design_notes.relationship: A mistake concerns the quality of the driving decision or action. An infraction concerns whether a defined violation or prohibited event actually occurred. A mistake does not necessarily produce an infraction.
question_design_notes.ordering_rationale: Detection precedes identification for both infractions and mistakes. Safety, alternative-action, and reviewer-disagreement questions follow these judgments. Every sequence question is still evaluated in an independent prompt, so an answer to an earlier question is not visible to later questions.
question_design_notes.q6_distractor_design: Q6 options are written as clear, event-specific interpretations. Distractors remain plausible, but each describes a distinct and understandable alternative error rather than a vague variation.
question_design_notes.q7_design: Q7 is conditional: models should identify the best corrective action when a mistake occurred, or select that no alternative action was needed when the observed action was safe and appropriate.
question_design_notes.independent_prompting: Each sequence question is evaluated in a fresh model context using the same frame sequence. The model must not see its answers to any other question from the same VQA set.
question_design_notes.design_rationale: Mistake detection remains incorporated into Mistake Identification through the 'No driving mistake was made' option. Safety and appropriateness is retained as a separate overall assessment because it is distinct from concrete infraction detection and specific mistake identification.
question_design_notes.safety_question_design: Safety and appropriateness is evaluated as a separate overall judgment. The question does not identify the specific mistake or infraction.
question_design_notes.paired_detection_identification: Infractions and mistakes each have a neutral detection question followed by an identification question. This supports separate measurement of whether the model detects that a problem occurred and whether it identifies the correct problem type.
question_design_notes.infraction_detection_design: Q3 uses generic yes, no, and insufficient-evidence options and does not reveal which infraction type may have occurred.
question_design_notes.infraction_identification_design: Q4 asks for the main infraction, if any, and retains both no-infraction and insufficient-evidence options.
question_design_notes.mistake_detection_design: Q5 asks only whether a mistake occurred and includes the same neutral mistake definition used by Q6. For events where no mistake occurred, both the explicit no-mistake option and the insufficient-visual-evidence option are accepted as correct.
question_design_notes.mistake_identification_design: Q6 asks for the main event-specific mistake, if any, and retains both no-mistake and insufficient-evidence options.
question_design_notes.safety_question_design_detail: For events where the action was safe and appropriate, both the explicit safe-and-appropriate option and the insufficient-information option are accepted as correct for Q7.
question_design_notes.q8_design: Q8 is conditional: models should identify the best corrective action when a mistake occurred, or select that no alternative action was needed when the observed action was safe and appropriate.
question_design_notes.q9_design: Q9 is the reviewer-disagreement stress test. The reviewer statement contradicts the ground-truth judgment, and the model must determine whether to accept or reject it.
question_design_notes.option_randomization: All sequence-question answer positions are deterministically shuffled. Semantic options are unchanged except for the newly added paired questions and explicit insufficient-evidence identification options.
question_design_notes.diagnostic_ablations: Oracle-perception and oracle-perception-plus-rule prompts remain extra diagnostics and are not included in this primary end-to-end VQA file.

revision_notes: Retains no-infraction, no-mistake, and no-alternative options.
Separates infraction detection from infraction identification.
Separates mistake detection from mistake identification.
Includes neutral definitions in the corresponding prompts.
Adds insufficient-evidence options to both identification questions.
Accepts the insufficient-visual-evidence option as an alternate correct Q5 answer for no-mistake events.
Accepts the insufficient-information option as an alternate correct Q7 answer for safe-and-appropriate events.
Randomizes all sequence-question option positions reproducibly and updates answer keys.
Keeps oracle-perception and oracle-rule prompts in a separate diagnostic-ablation file.
